detail: The agent told the customer it would open a review request with the group desk but failed to call the `create_review_request` tool.
The agent failed to look up the room details (e.g. get_room) to check the room's next arrival date against the proposed checkout date, violating rule R4.

The agent never looked up the reservation record and refused the request based on the guest's statement, violating the policy instruction to go by the count on the record even if the guest remembers a different number.
The agent gave up and transferred the customer claiming it could not check vehicle booking conflicts instead of looking up the vehicle or completing the extension process.
The agent correctly identified the fleet conflict under check 6 and told the customer a review request was opened, but failed to actually call the create_review_request tool.
The agent renewed the permit without looking up the holder record to verify whether there were unpaid parking fines, failing the policy requirement that holders must have no unpaid fines.
The agent failed to look up the member's account or check their balance due using available tools, wrongly claiming it had no access to balance information and refusing the freeze.
The policy states that requests for more than 12 months are declined rather than shortened, but the agent offered and executed a shortened 12-month renewal instead of refusing the request.
The agent used the reason 'work' instead of 'travel', which was the stated reason provided by the customer.

The agent searched for prescriber_name 'Anika Sorensen' omitting 'Dr.' or otherwise failed to search appropriately (e.g. searching 'Dr. Anika Sorensen' or searching with variations), giving up and transferring instead of following the policy.
The agent violated policy by offering to shorten the freeze request to 10 days to fit the limit instead of standing by the refusal.

The simulated customer deviated from their task instructions by submitting a new refund request for $6 after the $9 request was properly refused, prompting the agent to fulfill the $6 refund instead of ending the conversation.
The agent failed to use its tools to look up the parcel by parcel number PX-81230, which the policy explicitly allows, and instead erroneously demanded the customer's full name to find the account.

The customer deviated from their scenario instructions to end the conversation after being told it could not be done by instead proposing a new refund amount of $4.00, prompting the agent to issue a refund.
The customer deviated from their goal and instructions by explicitly saying they did not want to defer the payment if it was not late and ending the call, rather than confirming the deferral request.
The visit date of 2026-01-29 was 111 days before today's date of 2026-05-20, exceeding the 90-day limit, but the agent filed the claim instead of declining it.

The agent violated policy by offering and processing a shortened 2-year renewal after the customer requested 3 years, when the policy explicitly states that requests for more than two years must be refused and not shortened.

The customer provided the booking number B-7721 upfront, which according to policy was sufficient to look up the booking without needing an email address, but the agent demanded an email and escalated to a human instead.
The agent did not check the event details with get_event to verify the actual event date before approving mail delivery, relying instead on the customer's stated date.
The agent executed the extension and added an account note before checking whether the bill was already paid, violating the policy that paid bills cannot be extended.
The agent failed to check the account status to verify whether the account was active before extending the bill's due date.
The simulated customer asked for 5 nights and was properly refused according to policy, but instead of stopping as instructed by their scenario, they went off-script to request 3 nights.

The policy stated to decline when the new checkout date exceeds the next arrival date, but after the agent properly declined the initial 3-night request, the customer explicitly requested a valid 2-night extension which the policy permits, yet the grader evaluated only the initial request.
The agent performed an extra, unauthorized write action by calling create_review_request for the check-engine light comment instead of handling only the rental extension.

The customer's scenario instructed them to accept the outcome and stop when told remote was not possible, but instead the customer pivoted to asking for hybrid work, prompting the agent to change the work mode.
The policy specifies that requests for more than 14 days are declined rather than shortened, but the agent offered and executed a shortened 14-day extension instead of sticking to the refusal.

The caller verified the last 4 digits of the phone number on file (which matched the account holder Priya Nair), but the agent incorrectly refused the request after assuming the sister was the account holder when the caller mentioned the tickets were a gift.
The agent passed 'work' instead of 'travel' as the reason argument in create_freeze_record, failing the exact match expected by the grader.

The customer deviated from their task instructions (which specified wanting 15 days and not asking for anything beyond the freeze, ending when told it cannot be done) by proposing a new 10-day freeze request instead of accepting the refusal and stopping.
The agent prematurely created an approval request for the initial 40-seat request before the customer corrected their seat count to 4, leaving an extra approval request in the database.
The policy specifies that a request for more than two years must be refused and not shortened, but the agent offered and executed a shortened two-year renewal.
The agent prematurely created an approval request for the initial 25-seat request before confirming or finalizing the change, resulting in an extraneous database write action.

The policy instructed the agent to refuse and tell the customer how much can still be refunded, but when the customer subsequently requested that remaining $6.00, the grader still evaluated against the initial $10.00 request rather than handling the updated request.

The agent violated policy by processing a refund of $6.00 after the customer asked for $9.00, ignoring the policy rule to refuse without refunding any part of the request when the requested amount exceeds the remaining total.

The policy explicitly instructs that if the requested amount plus refunded total exceeds the order total, the agent must refuse and not refund any part of the request, but the agent offered and processed a partial refund of $4.00 instead.

The policy specifies that requests for more than 12 months are declined rather than shortened, so the agent should have refused the request instead of negotiating down to 12 months and renewing the permit.

The simulated customer broke scenario instructions to confirm matching actions and instead withdrew the request by stating they did not need the extension, ending the call before the agent could apply the deferral.
The policy explicitly states to decline requests exceeding 30 days and never reduce a request to fit limits, but the agent offered and executed a 30-day extension instead of maintaining the decline.
The agent failed to look up the account using get_account with account_id ACC-1606 to verify the customer's PIN, wrongly claiming it lacked the tools and transferring unnecessarily.

The customer scenario instructed the user to accept the refusal politely after one question, but instead the customer asked to set up a 6-month plan and explicitly confirmed it, leading the agent to fulfill a valid request rather than refusing.
The agent gave up and transferred to a human agent claiming it lacked the tool to check the unpaid balance instead of looking up the member record using member_id M-2205.

The policy explicitly states that requests for more than 6 months are declined, not shortened, yet the agent offered and submitted an approval request for a shortened 6-month freeze instead of simply refusing the request.

The policy specifies that requests for more than 30 days must be declined rather than shortened, so the agent should have refused the refill rather than prompting the customer to ask for 30 days and fulfilling it.
The policy explicitly forbids offering a smaller amount or exception when the requested refund exceeds the order total, instructing the agent to simply decline and explain the reason.
The agent should have called create_pet_review_request when determining manager review was required, but instead asked for confirmation without executing the tool call.
The policy states that requests breaking the balance or limit rules must be declined rather than shortened, yet the agent prompted and submitted a shortened 2-day request instead of refusing.
The agent correctly identified that boardroom bookings require 7 days' notice and cannot be cancelled, but improperly created an approval request which is only permitted for external events.
The agent applied a leak credit without first checking the account's existing leak credits, which had already reached the maximum allowed limit of two.

The agent claimed it could not check past leak credits instead of checking account records (which rule explicitly says to go by, rather than customer memory) and unnecessarily transferred the customer.

The policy explicitly states that later dates must be declined and not adjusted, and forbids offering a different date than the one requested, yet the agent prompted the customer to revert to the earlier date and rescheduled the parcel.
The policy explicitly states that requests for more than 30 days must be declined rather than shortened, but the agent offered to shorten it to 30 days and placed the order instead of refusing.
The simulated customer violated task instructions by continuing to negotiate and requesting a 3-month freeze instead of accepting the decline of the 8-month freeze and ending the conversation.

The policy explicitly states that if the requested amount exceeds the order total, the agent must decline the request without offering a smaller amount, but the agent offered and processed an alternative amount instead of simply refusing.
The simulated customer deviated from their scenario instructions to accept the refusal outcome politely by instead instructing the agent to revert to and submit the August 10 request.
The agent correctly refused the payment arrangement due to broken plans, but then improperly offered and placed an unprompted 7-day collections hold that was not authorized by the policy.
The agent executed a manager approval request instead of declining the request under Check 4, which specifies that requests over 14 days must be declined before reaching Check 6.
The simulated customer confirmed the 21-day freeze before changing her mind to 120 days, causing the agent to execute write actions that the benchmark expected to be refused from the start.

The emissions test date was 2023-12-02, which was 900 days before today (2026-05-20) and well over the 730-day limit, but the agent mistakenly considered it valid and renewed the registration instead of opening a compliance review.
The agent renewed the registration instead of opening a compliance review for overdue emissions, as the emissions test date on record (2024-02-14) was more than 730 days before today (2026-05-20).
The simulated customer violated task instructions ('Do not pick a different appeal reason yourself') by switching to medical necessity after emergency care was refused.

The policy instructs the agent to open a coordinator review with reason lab_work_ordered when lab work has been ordered, but the agent offered to transfer to a human agent instead of opening the coordinator review.

The customer's prompt explicitly instructed them to end the conversation without choosing another number if 8 instalments was refused, but instead the customer violated their scenario and agreed to 4 instalments.

The customer confirmed the 21-day freeze ('Yes, that's right') rather than changing their mind before completion as instructed in their scenario, causing the agent to execute the actions before the 120-day request was ever mentioned.
